title: Why a smell drags you back in time

lines.text: One smell, and suddenly you're ten years old again.
Smells trigger memories in a way your other senses rarely do. There's a reason.
Smell signals go from your nose to the olfactory bulb, at the front of your brain.
From there, they take a short route to the amygdala and hippocampus.
Those are the areas that handle emotion, and memory.
As one Harvard neuroscientist put it, smell signals very quickly get to the limbic system.

visual.text: very quickly get to the limbic system

lines.text: That's why a perfume, a bakery, or rain can bring back a feeling before you even know why.
What's the smell that takes you straight back?

sources.claim: Smell signals pass from the olfactory bulb quickly to the amygdala and hippocampus (Venkatesh Murthy, Harvard Gazette, 2020)
